1.why: All text uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line height, though letter spacing is standard rather than notably generous.

2.why: Instructions are sentence-case with no italics and no dense paragraphs; the only all-caps string is the setup secret itself, not instructional text.

3.why: Content sits in a narrow single column with full-width buttons and large text that should translate well to phone widths, although only desktop-sized screenshots were provided.

4.why: Each screen's guidance is a single short plain-language sentence, e.g. 'Use an authenticator app for payment approvals.'

5.why: The six-digit code field shows no placeholder or sample example, and the login fields contain pre-filled actual values rather than examples of expected input.

6.why: The longest passage on any screen is two lines, so the user is never forced to read a long block of text to proceed.

7.why: The 32-character secret is rendered as static text that could be selected and copied, but no copy button is provided and the wording explicitly directs manual entry.

8.why: No QR code or scannable equivalent appears on any screen; the setup page offers manual entry only.

9.why: There is no observable autofill or password-manager support: the OTP field is a plain input with no one-time-code hint, and the pre-filled login values appear app-supplied rather than autofilled.

10.why: Each screen has a bold heading and one full-width blue button that stand out clearly, though no step-progress indicator (e.g. 'Step 2 of 4') is shown.

11.why: Every screen requests a single primary action, with 'Log out' consistently styled as a subdued secondary button.

12.why: Screens advance to the next task and a developer-oriented log records events ('Authenticator provisioning created'), but the main UI never plainly summarises what just happened.

13.why: After the failed attempt the form remains intact and invites retry with no lockout or penalty shown, although no reveal/hide or re-request controls exist.

14.why: The error 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' is non-blaming but generic, failing to state that the code was wrong or expired or how to fix it.

15.why: No countdown, reading timeout, or session expiry is visible and a wrong code can simply be retried; the only implicit limit is the rotating time-based code window.
